name: Delhi–Amritsar–Katra Expressway

route.start: Jasaur Kheri (KMP Expressway), Jhajjar district, Haryana

timeline.event: The roughly 135 km Haryana stretch, from the KMP Expressway to the Punjab border near Kaithal, opens to traffic
Prime Minister inaugurates about 188 km — the Haryana packages and a 31 km stretch near Jalandhar (17 July)

history: This expressway is being built so that people can drive from Delhi to Amritsar in about four hours and to Katra — the base town for the Vaishno Devi shrine — in about six. It starts from the KMP Expressway near Delhi and runs as a brand-new road across Haryana and Punjab, with a branch near Nakodar that goes to Amritsar. The Haryana part is already open to traffic, while much of the Punjab and Jammu section is still being built.
facts: Planned total length is about 669 km, making it one of India's longest expressway projects.
A roughly 99 km branch leaves the main road near Nakodar and heads to Amritsar.
The 135 km Haryana stretch opened to traffic in 2024.
Being built by NHAI under the Bharatmala programme.
Will end at Katra, the gateway town to the Vaishno Devi shrine.
